generated_from.description: Started by todo_sync.py init; items added by todo_sync.py add from open GitHub issues.

ranking_method.score: value / sqrt(cost), multiplied by (1 + unblock_bonus) when the item unblocks at least one item
tie_breakers: primary source type, where the primary source is sources[0]: gh_issue, then impl_stub, then research_folder
primary source ref: issue number ascending for gh_issue, otherwise the ref path in code-point order
primary source item text in code-point order (absent item sorts first)

impact_definitions.silent_wrong_output: A shipped path completes without error or warning and publishes a value or feature that is wrong under an established rule.
impact_definitions.data_correctness: Output or reference data can be wrong or ungoverned, but the correct value still needs a rule or decision to define it, a guard is missing, or the wrong value already surfaces with a warning or error.
impact_definitions.runtime_failure: A path raises or aborts on an input it accepts.
impact_definitions.dev_velocity: Tests, CI or developer tooling are slower, noisier or less trustworthy than they need to be; no output changes.
impact_definitions.maintainability: Structure, duplication, dead code, missing tests or latent defects that no current production path reaches; no output changes.
impact_definitions.docs_tooling: Documentation, research records, configuration or agent tooling outside the shipped paths.

severity_scale.1: Cosmetic or hygiene: renames, dead code, stale docs, a test gap for working or accepted behavior.
severity_scale.2: Debt with a concrete cost, a latent defect that no current path reaches, a missing guard, or a defect that needs a rare or optional input.
severity_scale.3: A wrong or failing result on a supported but uncommon input, or a defect a warning already surfaces.
severity_scale.4: Wrong published output on a common input of a production path, or a failure that blocks a supported workflow.
severity_scale.5: Crashes or corrupts a production path on its normal inputs.

ranking_method.notes: Each item's severity, impact, LoE and blast radius come from its source's triage. Ranking compares scores rounded to 4 decimals; the tie breakers apply in order, so ids and ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone.

items.title: branch-commit-msg: describe a two-ref range (merge base of REF1 and REF2 up to REF2)
items.decision_question: Today `--base REF` (and a bare REF) is the merge base itself (plugins/harness/skills/branch-commit-msg/SKILL.md:43). The issue makes `--base` the tip ref when `--merge-base` is given, and reads two positionals as merge-base then base. Keep `--base` meaning the merge base and name the tip differently (for example `--tip`), or change `--base` as the issue writes it?
items.summary: The issue asks branch-commit-msg to take `--merge-base <ref> --base <ref2>` and capture `git diff $(git merge-base ref ref2)..ref2`, with two positionals read as merge-base then base and one positional as base. Checked: the skill accepts `[REF] [--base REF]` (plugins/harness/skills/branch-commit-msg/SKILL.md:4) where REF is one ref used as the merge base (:43); plugins/harness/scripts/branch_commit_msg.py:255-259 resolves that one ref and capture_branch (:153-159) captures every path differing from it, committed, staged, unstaged and untracked, so there is no committed-range-only capture between two refs. The flag name clashes with the current meaning of `--base`. Unverified: whether amend-commit-msg and merge-commit-msg need the same argument.
items.proposed_change: Settle the flag naming. Then add a two-ref mode to branch_commit_msg.py capture: resolve merge-base(REF1, REF2), capture only the committed paths in that range (no worktree, no untracked), store both SHAs in the skeleton and the TXT suffix, and accept two positionals; update the SKILL.md argument-hint and table, and add tests for the one- and two-positional forms.

blast_radius.reasoning: Changes the capture arguments and skeleton of branch-commit-msg; amend-commit-msg reads the same skeleton and TXT names.

loe.reasoning: A new capture mode over a committed range, argument parsing for two positionals, a suffix rule for two refs, docs and tests.

items.title: Audit pr-review and parallel2 dispatch for shared fixtures and cross-improvements
items.summary: The issue asks for an audit of the pr-review reviewer and fixer dispatch against parallel2 to find improvements for either and fixtures or resources they could share. Checked: parallel2 dispatches lanes from plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/parallel_lanes.py (render_brief :416-426) and reviews returned lanes with an unspecified spec-compliance and code-quality reviewer (plugins/harness/skills/parallel2/SKILL.md:64-66), while pr-review has its own reviewer and fixer agents; #137 and #140 name the same parallel2 gaps from the retirement side. Unverified: which pr-review pieces are reusable; no audit has been done.
items.proposed_change: Compare the two skills' dispatch, brief, model choice and review steps; write the findings as a short research note listing what parallel2 could reuse from pr-review (reviewer prompts, rubric, fix loop) and the reverse, then file or fold the concrete changes into #137 and #140.

blast_radius.reasoning: An audit that produces a note; code changes are filed separately.

loe.reasoning: Reading two large skills (pr-review SKILL.md is 76,148 bytes) and their agents and drivers.

items.why_ranked: Severity 1 hygiene audit, maintainability impact, M size.
